subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Net Metering: Selling Power Back
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Net Metering: Selling Power Back.

hook.text: Put solar panels on your roof and your meter can run backward.

buildup.text: When panels produce more than you use, excess flows back into the grid.

discovery.text: Net metering credits you for every kilowatt-hour you export. Your bill shrinks.

twist.text: Utilities argue rooftop solar shifts grid costs onto non-solar customers.

climax.text: Many regions now cap net metering or pay wholesale instead of retail rates.

punchline.text: Your roof becomes a tiny power plant — if the rules allow it.

quiz.question: What is the main criticism of net metering?
options: Solar panels produce too much power for the grid to handle
Grid maintenance costs shift onto customers without solar panels
Net metering causes voltage spikes in the distribution system
